images.title: Destitute pea pickers in California. Mother of seven children. Age thirty-two. Nipomo, California (Migrant Mother)

sources.title: Dorothea Lange's "Migrant Mother" Photographs in the Farm Security Administration Collection – Research Guide
sources.excerpt: I saw and approached the hungry and desperate mother, as if drawn by a magnet. I do not remember how I explained my presence or my camera to her, but I do remember she asked me no questions. I made five exposures, working closer and closer from the same direction.
sources.author: Dorothea Lange (1960, zitiert von der Library of Congress)

sources.title: Migrant Mother Series of Images – Research Guide
sources.excerpt: Note: This is an unretouched version of image #1, and shows a thumb in the immediate foreground on the right side.
sources.author: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division

images.title: Raising the Flag on Iwo Jima

sources.title: Was the Flag-Raising on Iwo Jima Posed? (American Heritage, Vol. 68, Issue 6)
sources.excerpt: Rosenthal stood only 5-foot-4, so he perched on a makeshift pile of sandbags and rocks to get a better angle. Just as he felt that he was set, he saw movement in his peripheral vision - the replacement flag was being raised by five Marines and a Navy corpsman.
sources.author: American Heritage

images.title: Road works and Fuji near Kawaguchiko (Red Fuji)

sources.title: Making the Image: Red Mount Fuji – Chris Steele-Perkins (Magnum Photos; Eintrag aus „Magnum Contact Sheets“)
sources.excerpt: The idea for the project started when Miyako gave me a book of Hokusai's prints, 36 Views of Mount Fuji. I was struck by the documentary nature of his images, which depict views of ordinary life, with the mountain as a presence in the background.
sources.author: Chris Steele-Perkins

sources.title: Mark Power: Contact Sheet Warsaw Dalmatian (Magnum Photos; Eintrag aus „Magnum Contact Sheets“)
sources.excerpt: This contact sheet contains my'Dalmatian' picture, perhaps the most recognizable photograph from the series. It was a remarkable slice of good fortune.
sources.author: Mark Power

images.title: Woman looking at herself in store window, New York City
images.location: Madison Avenue, New York City, USA

sources.title: Contact Sheet: Richard Kalvar – Woman in Window (Magnum Photos; Eintrag aus „Magnum Contact Sheets“)
sources.excerpt: If I had wanted a funny little photograph of people looking through a window, frame 27A would have fit the bill. But what has always excited me in photography is to step out of'real' reality and enter a world of frozen dreams, abstracted from the ordinary.
sources.author: Richard Kalvar

sources.title: Behind the Image: René Burri's São Paulo (Magnum Photos)
sources.excerpt: Each line, shape and shadow in the image contributes to a dense visual universe, filling the entire frame - a lesson he took from Henri Cartier-Bresson - from the vertiginous ridges of the buildings to the street lines below.
sources.author: Magnum Photos

images.title: New York City (Bulldog)
images.location: Upper West Side, New York City, USA

sources.title: Contact Sheet Prints – Elliott Erwitt, Bulldog in New York (Magnum Photos)
sources.excerpt: The contact shows Erwitt's patience, shooting around an image methodically until he has all the elements synchronized for maximum effect. As he says,'It's a lot of pictures getting to the good one.'
sources.author: Magnum Photos / Elliott Erwitt

sources.title: Behind the Image: An English Sunny Afternoon – Ian Berry (Magnum Photos)
sources.excerpt: In the 1970s, Ian Berry set out to create a portrait of English life. The English is a document of culture and traditions during a transitional time.
sources.author: Magnum Photos

sources.title: Alex Webb's best photograph: children in Tehuantepec, Mexico (The Guardian)
sources.excerpt: It wasn't until later that I realised there was a second ball in the frame: a basketball falling through a hoop. This kind of photography - wandering the streets, exploring the world with few preconceptions - is so much about immediacy, intuition and serendipity.
sources.author: Alex Webb (im Gespräch mit The Guardian)
